title: Gangtok shared taxi stands: which one goes where
meta_description: Deorali, Vajra, Lal Bazaar, Children's Park, Ranka stand and the SNT bus stand: where Gangtok's shared taxis leave for each town, seat fares and timings.
summary: Gangtok has no single bus station. Shared taxis to Siliguri, NJP, Kalimpong and Darjeeling use the Deorali stand on NH10; North Sikkim jeeps use the Vajra stand; West and South Sikkim jeeps leave from below MG Marg; short town runs leave from Lal Bazaar and Children's Park. Seats cost ₹20–600, indicative 2026.

sections.heading: How Gangtok's shared taxis work
paras: Shared taxis are how Sikkim moves. Gangtok has very few city buses, and most locals ride in shared Maruti vans, Boleros, Sumos and Scorpios that leave when every seat is filled. Long-distance jeeps usually carry 8–10 passengers; town taxis take 4–5. Fares for the main routes are fixed by the state and posted at the bigger stands, so you pay the same as the person beside you.

Each part of Sikkim has its own stand, spread along the town's steep roads. That is the single most confusing thing for first-time visitors, and it is why a driver at the wrong stand will tell you, correctly, that nothing goes to Pelling from here. Stands also move when the town opens a new parking complex. Our table is how we understand the layout in 2026; ask your hotel the evening before you travel, and check current status before you travel.

At the bigger stands you buy a ticket at a counter, often a day ahead in season, and the ticket shows a seat number and the vehicle number. At smaller stands you simply tell the driver where you are going and wait for the car to fill. Children who sit on a lap usually travel free; a child who needs a seat pays the full fare. If you are in a hurry and the jeep is two seats short, the other passengers may agree to share the cost of the empty seats so you can leave.

paras: Use this table to pick the stand before you pick the time. Fares are per seat, one way, indicative 2026, and rise a little with fuel prices.

sections.heading: Deorali: arriving and leaving Sikkim
paras: Almost every shared jeep from Siliguri, NJP and Kalimpong ends its run at Deorali, on the highway about 2 km below the town centre. It is also where you catch one back down. The stand is busy from about 6 am, and departures to Siliguri are most frequent before noon. By mid-afternoon, seats get scarce and drivers start offering the whole car instead.

From Deorali, take a local shared taxi up to MG Marg or Paljor Stadium Road for ₹20–40 a seat, or a reserved taxi for ₹150–300, indicative 2026. Porters will offer to carry bags up the steps for a fee; agree the price first. The Gangtok ropeway's lower station is also at Deorali, though it runs up to the Secretariat area rather than to MG Marg.

For Siliguri, a seat costs ₹400–600 and the drive takes 4–5 hours, longer when NH10 is broken. For Darjeeling, expect ₹400–600 and 4–5 hours; for Kalimpong, ₹250–400 and about 3 hours. Buy your seat at the counter, not from someone on the road, and ask for a seat number.

If you arrive with heavy bags, consider staying a short taxi ride from Deorali rather than hauling suitcases up the steep lanes near MG Marg. Many travellers do the reverse: they leave luggage at the hotel, travel light for a day trip, and only take the big bags on the final morning to Deorali.

sections.heading: Vajra stand and North Sikkim
paras: The North Sikkim taxi stand, known to everyone as Vajra stand after the Vajra cinema hall beside it, is a multi-storey building with parking for jeeps. Shared jeeps run from here to Phodong, Kabi, Mangan and other towns on the North Sikkim Highway, mostly in the morning. Seats to Mangan cost about ₹200–350, indicative 2026.

Lachung, Lachen, Yumthang and Gurudongmar are a different matter. They need a protected area permit and are visited on packaged tours in permit-registered vehicles, so you book through an agent rather than walk up for a seat. The tour vehicles often start from Vajra stand. North Sikkim permits were suspended for weeks after landslides in 2025 and can be stopped again at short notice; check current status before you travel.
Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La shared tours also gather at Vajra stand or at the agent's office. Your agent will tell you where to be and when, usually between 7 and 8 am.

sections.heading: West, South and short local runs
paras: For Pelling, Gyalshing, Namchi and Ravangla, shared jeeps leave from the stand below MG Marg where the road turns towards Tibet Road. Most go before noon. Expect ₹350–500 to Pelling (5–6 hours), ₹200–300 to Namchi (about 3 hours) and ₹250–350 to Ravangla, indicative 2026. SNT also runs morning buses on these routes from its Paljor Stadium Road stand at slightly lower fares.

For Ranka and Lingdum Monastery, use the Ranka stand on Paljor Stadium Road in Arithang. For Rumtek, shared taxis run mainly in the late morning and early afternoon at ₹60–120 a seat; ask your hotel which stand is in use, as this has shifted over the years. For Tashi View Point, Penlong and the Vajra side of town, the Children's Park stand next to MG Marg is quickest. Lal Bazaar's stand, on the ground floor of the Kanchendzonga Shopping Complex, serves town routes and nearby villages.

sections.heading: Tips from the jeep queue
paras: A few habits make shared travel in Sikkim easier, safer and a little cheaper.
list: Go early. Most long-distance jeeps leave between 6 am and 1 pm; afternoons are slow.
Buy two seats if you want space. Paying for the empty seat beside you is cheaper than reserving the car.
Ask for the front seat at the counter if you get carsick; it usually costs the same.
Bags go on the roof under a tarpaulin. Pack a rain cover and keep valuables and medicines with you.
Keep small notes. Drivers on town routes rarely have change for ₹500.
In town, flag down a shared taxi anywhere on its route and say where you are going before you get in.
In monsoon, ask the driver which way he is going. When NH10 is cut, jeeps may detour via Kalimpong, Rhenock or Pakyong, which adds hours and sometimes fare.

sections.heading: When a reserved car makes more sense
paras: Shared seats are the cheapest way to move between towns, but they are not always the best. For a family of four or five with luggage, a reserved car from Gangtok to Siliguri at ₹4,000–5,500 for a small car or ₹5,500–7,500 for an Innova, indicative 2026, can cost about the same as five seats plus porters and the taxi to and from the stand.

Reserve a car when you have an early flight from Bagdogra, when someone in the group is unwell or elderly, or when you are carrying a lot of shopping home. Book through your hotel or a registered stand counter and ask for the fixed fare in writing. Check current status before you travel, as fares are revised from time to time.

A middle path works well for small groups. Reserve a car for the transfer days, when you carry luggage and need to keep to a timetable, and use shared taxis for everything inside Gangtok and for the trips to Rumtek and Ranka. That way you pay for comfort only when it matters.

Whatever you choose, note the vehicle number before you set off, keep the driver's phone number, and tell your hotel your expected arrival time. Phone signal drops on parts of NH10 along the Teesta, and in Sikkim the people waiting for you will worry long before you do.

faqs.q: Where do shared jeeps to Siliguri leave from in Gangtok
faqs.a: From the Deorali (Mainline) taxi stand on NH10, about 2 km below MG Marg. Seats cost ₹400–600, indicative 2026, and the drive takes 4–5 hours, longer when NH10 is damaged. Go before noon for the most departures. A local shared taxi from MG Marg to Deorali costs ₹20–40 a seat. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which taxi stand in Gangtok is for North Sikkim
faqs.a: The North Sikkim taxi stand, known as Vajra stand, near the Vajra cinema hall. Shared jeeps run from here to Phodong, Kabi and Mangan. Lachung, Lachen and Gurudongmar need a permit and are visited on packaged tours booked through an agent, though many of those vehicles also start from Vajra. Check current status before you travel, since North Sikkim permits are often suspended.

faqs.q: How do I get a shared jeep from Gangtok to Pelling
faqs.a: Go to the stand below MG Marg at the turning towards Tibet Road, before about 11 am. A seat to Pelling costs about ₹350–500, indicative 2026, and the trip takes 5–6 hours. Some jeeps go only to Gyalshing, from where local jeeps run the last 10 km. SNT also runs morning buses from its Paljor Stadium Road stand. Ask your hotel to confirm the stand.

faqs.q: How much is a shared taxi within Gangtok
faqs.a: ₹20–40 a seat for most town routes, indicative 2026. Flag one down anywhere on its route, say where you are going before you get in, and pay when you get out. A reserved taxi for a short trip within town costs about ₹150–300. Keep small notes, because drivers on short routes rarely carry change for ₹500.

faqs.q: Where is the SNT bus stand in Gangtok
faqs.a: On Paljor Stadium Road, about 6–7 minutes' walk from MG Marg. Sikkim Nationalised Transport runs buses from here to Siliguri and to towns across Sikkim, mostly in the morning, at fares a little below shared jeeps. Buy tickets at the counter a day ahead in May, June and October. Timings change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I get to Rumtek by shared taxi
faqs.a: Shared taxis run to Rumtek mainly in the late morning and early afternoon, at about ₹60–120 a seat, indicative 2026. The stand has moved over the years, so ask your hotel which one is in use. The drive is about 24 km and takes 1 hour. A reserved return taxi costs ₹1,200–2,000 and lets you add Ranka and Lingdum on the way.

faqs.q: Can I get a shared jeep from Gangtok to Darjeeling
faqs.a: Yes, from the Deorali stand, mostly in the morning. Seats cost about ₹400–600, indicative 2026, and the trip takes 4–5 hours via NH10 and Teesta Bazaar or via Kalimpong. Fewer jeeps run on this route than to Siliguri, so buy your ticket the day before in season. Check current status before you travel during monsoon.

faqs.q: Do shared taxis run late at night in Gangtok
faqs.a: Long-distance jeeps rarely leave after mid-afternoon, and town shared taxis thin out after about 7–8 pm. After that you will need a reserved taxi, which costs more at night. If you arrive late from Siliguri, ask your hotel to send or book a taxi to meet you at Deorali, and agree the fare before you get in.

faqs.q: Can shared taxis take me to Tsomgo Lake
faqs.a: Not as an ordinary shared jeep. Tsomgo needs a protected area permit, so travel agents sell seats in permit-registered tour vehicles at ₹800–1,300 a seat, indicative 2026. Your hotel or a travel desk near MG Marg can book one. Vehicles usually leave between 7 and 8 am from the agent's office or Vajra stand. Check current status before you travel.
